messages:
Sam: noticing intermittent packet loss and huge east-west latency spikes between rack-a (az1) and rack-b (az1). Affected: dedicated GPU pool for inference (dgx-pool-2). Seen in both TCP and RDMA flows. ~5-12% packet loss, lots of retransmits and RDMA QP timeouts. Symptoms started ~15:20 UTC. :eyes:
Olivia: yikes. any obvious recent config changes on ToR or LB?
Sam: nothing from infra change log in the last 24h. No canary deploys either. Metrics show jump in p95 latency on inter-rack paths and per-pod connect failures to the model servers.
Raj: attaching quick counters from ToR-B-02: interface Gi1/0/10 RX errors and CRC on the peer-facing uplink. Also see MTU drop counters incrementing. Could be jumbo frame mismatch or firmware bug.
Raj: ```
# show int Gi1/0/10 counters
Gi1/0/10: RX errors: 1245, CRC: 312, TX errors: 2
MTU drops: 987
```
Anya: RDMA sensitive to MTU and fragmentation. If GPUDirect is in use, small MTU mismatches will surface as QP resets. Do we have any non-standard MTU changes staged?
Sam: default NIC MTU on hosts is 9000, but I see a couple older nodes in rack-b set at 1500 by accident (probably from last reprovision). Potential cause.
InfraBot: [alert] network.tor.packet_loss > 5% between rack-a and rack-b (alert id: NB-4821) — graphs: https://mon/redwood/alerts/NB-4821 :loudspeaker:
Leo: two parallel things to validate: 1) confirm MTU across all switches + hosts; 2) check L4 LB behaviour — if the internal L4 is SNATing or rebalancing flows, fragmentation could be happening mid-path. Also check GRO/GSO offload weirdness.
Olivia: can someone run a tcpdump and an ibdump on the host pair? need to see if frames are getting truncated or if there's a mid-path rewrite.
Raj: running packet capture on host gpu-node-12 -> gpu-node-27 now. Early dump shows ICMP fragmentation-needed from an intermediate hop and a couple of truncated RDMA packets. Snap: ```
17:22:03.123 IP 10.0.12.27 > 10.0.22.12: frag needed, mtu 1500
17:22:03.125 ib_pkt: QP 0x3a4 reset due to RNR timeout
```
Anya: that suggests MTU mismatch on the path — possibly a ToR uplink or a leaf switch with 1500. If ToR-B has uplink MTU 1500, jumbo frames from hosts at 9000 will get dropped.
Nora: ops note: if we push a mass MTU change or reboot ToR, we'll impact other services in az1. We should coordinate a short maintenance window if confirmed. Also GPU capacity will degrade if we cordon nodes. Cost impact estimate: if we lose 10% cluster capacity for 2 hours, projected infra spend impact ~ $1.2k (reserved + ephemeral bump).
Sam: temporary mitigation idea: set host NIC MTU down to 1500 on the affected hosts and retest RDMA flows. If that stabilizes, we can avoid ToR reboot in the short term. Any objections?
Leo: do it for a small canary (gpu-node-12/13). Command: ```sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500 && systemctl restart rdma```. Watch for side-effects.
Olivia: I'll open a vendor ticket for ToR firmware + ask for patch notes on MTU handling. Assign to raj + vendor.
Raj: canary MTU change started on gpu-node-12/13. Early telemetry: retransmits dropped to ~1% and RDMA QP resets decreased. Running load test against the model server.
Sam: great. Raj, keep captures running and collect ToR interface stats. Olivia, vendor ticket please. Anya, prepare rollback and a plan to standardize MTU across fleet (infra playbook). Nora, watch capacity and cost. I'll update on status in 30m. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: (automated) incident NB-4821 acknowledged by Sam. ETA next update 30m.
